From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: SIEM-ready audit export beta — scope + approval (delivery semantics messaging)

Marcus, Sean —

We’re at the point where we need a crisp beta approval on (a) scope and (b) how we describe delivery guarantees to customers.

Proposal for beta (high level):
- Destinations: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once (durable buffering, retry/backoff, explicit failure states)
- Filtering: include/exclude by event_type + actor + workspace/tenant + environment + time window (optionally IP/region if we can do it safely)
- Feature gated: per-tenant flag + allowlist

Customer-facing wording draft (key question):
We say “At-least-once delivery” and explicitly note duplicates are possible. We provide dedupe guidance using a stable event_id (and suggest downstream de-dupe in SIEM).

Can you both confirm this messaging is acceptable for beta (given duplicates and possible out-of-order), and call out any must-have conditions before we let Sales/CS onboard design partners?

Attachments:
- SIEM-ready Audit Export Beta PRD v0.9 (PDF)
- Customer-facing wording proposal — delivery guarantees (Google Doc link)

Thanks,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export beta — scope + approval (delivery semantics messaging)

Agree with at-least-once semantics for beta.

On messaging: we should be explicit that:
- Duplicates are possible and expected under retry/backoff.
- Ordering is best-effort; do not assume strict ordering across partitions.
- We provide a stable dedupe key (event_id) AND include request_id + emitted_at for correlation.

Two security conditions from my side before we onboard anyone:
1) Export destination config changes must themselves be audited (who changed what/when, including test delivery attempts).
2) Strong guardrails on destination configuration: validate endpoints, restrict dangerous configs (e.g., allowlist hostnames for Splunk if feasible), and never display secret material in the Console/API.

If those are already in the PRD, I’m good to approve the semantics + wording direction.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:28 AM PST
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export beta — scope + approval (delivery semantics messaging)

+1 on at-least-once messaging with explicit duplicates.

SRE must-haves before beta onboarding (esp. if Sales is positioning this as “SIEM-ready”):
- A visible destination health state in Console (enabled/paused/degraded) + last_success_at + last_error.
- Clear failure modes: if backlog grows beyond threshold, destination should auto-mark degraded and stop hammering the sink.
- Runbook + paging policy agreed (we can start with ticket-level alerts for beta if usage is tiny, but we need criteria).

Ask: can we avoid the phrase “reliably deliver exactly once” anywhere in docs/FAQ? I’ve seen it creep into enablement decks.

If we include a sentence like “at-least-once; duplicates possible; customer should dedupe on event_id” in every customer-facing doc (setup guides + release notes + FAQ), then I’m comfortable.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SIEM-ready audit export beta — scope + approval (delivery semantics messaging)

This is helpful, thank you.

Actions I’m taking based on your notes:
- Update PRD + FAQ language to remove any “exactly once” implication and add an explicit callout:
  “Delivery guarantee: at-least-once. Duplicates and occasional out-of-order delivery are possible. Dedupe on event_id.”
- Add requirement: audit export destination CRUD + test events are always written to audit log.
- Add requirement: destination validation + secret handling guardrails (no secrets displayed/returned).

Open question for both of you: do we want to use the term “at-least-once” in the Console UI (technical), or do we want to phrase it as “Duplicates possible; dedupe recommended” and link to docs?

(We’re getting mixed feedback from Solutions Eng: some customers understand “at-least-once,” others just want the operational implication.)

Naomi

For UI: I’d avoid leading with jargon.

Suggestion:
- UI label: “Delivery: duplicates possible (recommended: dedupe on event_id)”
- Docs/FAQ: use the formal term “at-least-once” once, then explain it.

That gives us correct semantics without relying on customer interpretation of distributed systems terms.

Marcus

Agree with Marcus.

One more nuance for docs (to avoid support escalations):
- Call out that “test event” is synthetic and clearly marked (so it doesn’t confuse compliance teams).
- Provide a short note on replay tooling: “Replays can produce duplicates; use with care.”

If those are in place + we have dashboards for backlog + error rate (even basic), I’m a yes on beta onboarding.

Sean

Closing the loop with updated decisions and asking for final “go” so I can greenlight beta onboarding for the first two design partners.

Decisions (per this thread):
1) Delivery semantics (customer-facing):
   - UI: “Delivery: duplicates possible (recommended: dedupe on event_id)” + link to docs
   - Docs/FAQ/release notes: “at-least-once delivery; duplicates and occasional out-of-order delivery are possible; dedupe on event_id”
   - We will not use “exactly-once” anywhere.

2) Security/SRE conditions we’re making hard requirements for beta:
   - Audit export config changes + test delivery attempts written to audit log
   - Destination validation guardrails + secrets never returned/displayed
   - Destination health states in Console + last_success_at/last_error
   - Backpressure behavior to prevent retry storms + clear degraded state
   - Docs: synthetic test event is clearly marked; replay produces duplicates; use with care

If you’re both comfortable with the above as the approval bar for beta onboarding, reply “Approved” and I’ll proceed.

Thanks,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
